title: Unfiltered: roasts, comebacks & real talk
entries: How a good roast works

Great roasts hit something true, specific and visible, then exaggerate it to absurdity. The target should laugh too. Generic insults ('you're ugly') are lazy; specific observations ('you dress like a substitute teacher who lost a bet') land.
Roast rules

Roast choices, not things people can't change. Avoid real trauma, race, disability and anything the person is genuinely insecure about. Punch up or sideways, never down. End with a little love so it stays a roast and not a fight.
Joke structure
Setup creates an expectation, punchline breaks it. Put the funniest word at the very end. Cut every word that isn't needed; brevity is the soul of the laugh.
Callbacks
Bringing back an earlier joke later, in a new context, gets bigger laughs than the original. Great for roasts and conversations.
Comeback craft
The best comebacks are calm, short and turn the insult around. Agreeing and exaggerating ('Yeah, and that's my good side') disarms people better than getting defensive.
Dark humor

Dark humor jokes about grim subjects (death, disaster, misery) to make them bearable. It works when the target is the absurdity of the situation, not victims. Timing and audience are everything; read the room first.
Swearing well

Profanity lands harder when it's used for emphasis, not as filler. One perfectly placed curse beats ten random ones. Creative swearing ('a dumpster fire wearing a trench coat') is funnier than repetition.
Sarcasm
Saying the opposite of what you mean, with a tone that signals it. In text it often reads as sincere or cruel, so exaggerate it or make it obviously absurd.
Self-deprecation
Joking about yourself first makes you likable and bulletproof: nobody can roast what you already roasted. Too much of it reads as insecurity.
Internet slang basics

Common terms: 'cap' / 'no cap' (lie / no lie), 'mid' (mediocre), 'rizz' (charm), 'delulu' (delusional), 'ate' (did amazingly), 'L' and 'W' (loss and win), 'ratio' (a reply getting more likes than the original), 'touch grass' (go outside and get perspective).
Frank dating truths

Attraction is more about confidence, humor, effort and how you make people feel than about looks alone. Being genuinely interested beats trying to be interesting. Neediness and constant validation-seeking kill attraction fast.
Texting someone you're into
Match their energy, don't triple-text, have actual conversations instead of endless 'wyd', and move to meeting up instead of becoming pen pals. Mystery is overrated; clarity is attractive.
Rejection
Rejection is information, not a verdict on your worth. Everyone attractive gets rejected all the time; they just keep going. The people who never get rejected never ask.
Breakups
No contact for a while helps you heal faster. Don't be friends right away. Focus on sleep, exercise, friends, and something you're building. Revisit what you learned, not what you lost.
Situationships
An undefined relationship usually stays undefined because one person likes it that way. If you want clarity, ask directly once; their answer and behavior after that is your answer.
Real talk on friendship
Real friends tell you when you're being an idiot, show up when it's inconvenient, and are happy when you win. Keep the ones who do; let the rest fade without drama.
Calling out BS
Ask for specifics ('what exactly do you mean?'), ask for evidence ('how do you know?'), and ask what would change their mind. BS usually collapses under three honest questions.
Excuses decoded
'I don't have time' often means 'it's not a priority'. 'I'll start Monday' often means 'I don't want to start'. 'It's complicated' often means 'I don't want to say'. Not always, but often.
Being blunt without being a jerk
Be honest about the thing, generous about the person. 'This plan has a huge hole' is blunt; 'you're an idiot' is just mean. Blunt people who are also clearly on your side are rare and valuable.
Hype vs truth
Good friends hype you up and tell you the truth. Hype without truth is flattery; truth without warmth is cruelty. VEX's job is both.
